auth.hook: Accounts and roles: profile, e-mail change by link, password, sessions, roles as data.

settings.hook: Configuration as data: a typed registry, user over workspace over global, and the price catalogue in dated versions; every change audited.

api-keys.hook: API keys created, rotated, revoked and authenticated; shown once, only a hash kept.

orazaka-client.hook: One Orazaka client for the TypeScript products: start a run, read its status and outputs, typed errors, a time limit and a circuit breaker.

webhooks.hook: Signed, idempotent webhooks, both ways: delivered with retries, verified and applied once.

organize.hook: A name, an avatar, tags and collections for any entity; and the workspace organised: tags with markers, status sets, saved views, bulk actions.

brief.hook: The weekly brief: a few figured recommendations, each with one action.

org.hook: The public facts about Krizaka in one validated JSON that every footer, site and app reads: legal identity, marks, live products, sites, footer line.

db.hook: The database foundation: shared types, transactions, module schemas embedded in the product’s own migrations, a test database.

privacy.hook: Loi 25: consents by purpose written once, export and erasure assembled from every module, retention set by the admin.

outbox.hook: The transactional outbox: written with the work, delivered at least once by leased workers, retried, then dead-lettered.

mail.hook: Queued mail sent after the commit, once per key, never to a suppressed address; the provider is the admin's choice; bounces and complaints suppress.

coupons.hook: Discount and credit coupons the admin manages: reserved under a lock, confirmed once, released when unpaid, refunded; partners for attribution.

credits.hook: One credits ledger: grants that expire with daily and monthly caps, purchases, holds and refunds, exact under concurrency.

payments.hook: Payments behind a port: checkout with discount terms, verified webhooks applied once, refunds and expiry, integer money.

rate-limit.hook: Limits per action: fixed windows per address and subject, set by the admin, counted exactly under concurrency.

time.hook: Date arithmetic on an instant, exact in any time zone: the facade the « Krizaka first » dates rule points to.

audit.hook: Who did what: an append-only trail in its own schema, inside the transaction or beside it, filtered, exported and redacted (Loi 25).

config.hook: The quality kit of every TypeScript repository: ESLint configs, the dependency-cruiser preset, tsconfig bases, Prettier and the debt ratchet.

hero.title: The TypeScript backend building blocks behind every Krizaka product
hero.lead: Accounts, settings, API keys, webhooks — written once, tested on a real PostgreSQL, published on npm. A product installs a package and writes only what is its own.

pillars.title: One implementation, no copies
pillars.lead: What every product used to rewrite lives in one place, with one author and one release.

ports.title: Ports, not frameworks
ports.text: No framework, no vendor SDK, no environment variable, no ambient clock: a package asks for a store, a mailer, a clock — you pass them in.

proven.title: Tested on the real thing
proven.text: Where a package stores, its integration test runs on PostgreSQL, and a store ships a contract kit that every adapter runs.

released.title: Versioned, published, readable
